final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the indispensable catalytic residue that forms the internal Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutating to alanine definitively abolishes CBS transsulfuration activity.
Arginine cannot form the requisite covalent aldimine linkage with PLP, reliably abolishing catalytic activity while maintaining minimal electrostatic disturbance.
G307S is the classical pathogenic homocystinuria variant that severely impairs catalytic competence without completely precluding stable protein folding.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 mutations definitively abolish CBS activity based on well-established catalytic and clinical mechanisms.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the essential catalytic residue forming the Schiff base with the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) cofactor; alanine substitution prevents aldimine formation and completely abolishes enzyme activity.
K119 is the essential catalytic lysine that forms the internal Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutating to alanine definitively abolishes enzymatic activity.
Arginine substitution at the catalytic Lys119 retains positive charge but cannot form the required covalent internal aldimine with PLP, effectively eliminating catalytic turnover.
While arginine retains positive charge, it cannot form the requisite aldimine link with PLP, reliably causing complete loss of catalytic function.
Gly307 is located within a conserved active-site loop; the pathogenic G307S substitution causes classic B6-unresponsive homocystinuria with virtually complete loss of enzymatic activity.
G307S is the clinically validated Celtic homocystinuria mutation that causes near-total loss of catalytic activity without entirely destabilizing protein synthesis.
Ile278 is a critical core residue in the catalytic domain; the classic homocystinuria mutation I278T severely impairs catalytic function.
I278T is the most frequent pathogenic loss-of-function allele, severely disrupting active site architecture and transsulfuration activity.
Thr191 is an active-site adjacent residue where the pathogenic T191M mutation drastically compromises catalytic activity to near-undetectable levels.
T191M disrupts key loop dynamics near the catalytic pocket, causing severe loss of CBS function in human homocystinuria.
Cys52 serves as an axial ligand coordinating the regulatory heme iron; disruption of coordination perturbs active conformation and catalytic function.
C52 is an axial heme ligand whose loss disrupts regulatory heme binding, but enzyme basal activity can partially persist.
His65 is the opposing axial ligand to the heme iron; alanine substitution impairs proper heme coordination and significantly reduces enzymatic activity.
H65 coordinates the regulatory heme; disrupting it impairs redox sensing, though transsulfuration catalytic machinery remains largely intact.
Side-chain introduction at Gly307 in the tightly packed active-site loop sterically impairs substrate positioning and reduces catalytic turnover.
Alanine substitution at G307 introduces steric clash but is less polar and disruptive than the classic pathogenic G307S substitution.
